foodDescription: Dense, slightly sweet dark rye bread, baked on maple or calamus leaves. Served with almost every meal.
Large gray peas cooked and topped with fried bacon and onion, eaten with kefir. The national dish, especially at Christmas.
Small crescent-shaped buns filled with bacon and onion. Sold in every bakery, and made in huge batches for celebrations.
Small fish smoked over alder and packed in oil in flat tins. Riga sprats were a Soviet delicacy and are still a national export.
Salted herring with boiled potatoes and soft cottage cheese mixed with sour cream and dill.
A small open tart of rye pastry filled with mashed potato and sweet carrot, from the Courland region. Protected by the EU as a traditional specialty.
A mild fresh cheese with caraway seeds, made for Jāņi, the midsummer festival on June 23 and 24, and eaten with beer.
A sweet dessert of rye bread soaked and cooked with dried fruit and spices, topped with whipped cream.
A small bar of sweet curd cheese coated in chocolate, sold in every supermarket fridge. A childhood favorite.
A black herbal liqueur made in Riga since 1752 from a secret recipe of herbs, roots, and berries. Usually mixed into coffee or black currant juice.
A slightly fizzy, slightly sour drink fermented from rye bread. Sold cold in summer.
Latvia brews many small-batch beers, and Riga has several craft brewery bars. Beer is part of the Jāņi celebrations.
